stories.head: Infillion acquires Foursquare's 16 billion check-in dataset
stories.plain: Infillion is buying Foursquare's massive location check-in database — 16 billion data points on where real people go. This kind of first-party location data is increasingly rare and valuable as cookies disappear, and it directly affects how ad targeting and customer data platforms are built and priced going forward.

stories.head: Fingerprint maps how AI crawlers access the web
stories.plain: Fingerprint has published research tracking how AI crawlers scrape and index web content. For marketers, understanding which bots see your content and how is now essential to being cited inside AI-generated answers. This is a practical resource for anyone trying to improve generative engine optimization strategy.

stories.head: Taboola bids for finance-focused ad network Dianomi
stories.plain: Taboola is moving to acquire Dianomi, a native ad network specializing in financial services audiences. If completed, this consolidates two major content recommendation players and gives Taboola a premium finance vertical — shifting how brands in regulated industries buy programmatic placements and who controls those customer engagement surfaces.

stories.head: Guy Gunter Home builds one e-commerce platform for both B2B and B2C buyers
stories.plain: This case study shows how a home furnishings brand rebuilt its digital store to serve wholesale trade buyers and retail consumers from a single platform. The key lesson: smart personalization logic can serve fundamentally different buying modes without splitting your tech stack — a useful model for brands managing dual commerce channels.

stories.head: Toggl adds 'Time Intelligence' layer to flag margin risk and capacity strain in real time
stories.plain: Toggl's new feature moves beyond simple hour logging to surface automated alerts about delivery risk and profit margin erosion before projects go off track. For agency and consultancy operations teams, this is an early example of agentic decisioning applied to resource management — the system spots problems and flags action without waiting for a human review.

stories.head: HubSpot rebuilds its platform around AI agents
stories.plain: HubSpot has redesigned its entire platform so a Breeze Assistant coordinates AI agents across sales, marketing, and service — all fed by a self-updating CRM. This is a major architectural shift, not a feature add, signalling that agentic systems are now the core product at one of the market's largest CRM vendors.

stories.head: AI is telling consumers not to buy your product
stories.plain: A new study finds 81% of shoppers using AI chatbots have abandoned a purchase based on the chatbot's guidance. This flips the assumption that AI shopping assistants help brands sell more — and raises urgent questions about how brands optimise their presence inside AI-generated answers.

stories.head: Does anyone understand the CDP market anymore?
stories.plain: BlueConic's CEO explains how three years of AI agent integration and M&A activity have reshaped the CDP category almost beyond recognition. Buyers now face a market where classic CDPs, data warehouses, and agent orchestration platforms all claim the same territory — a buying decision that is genuinely harder than it used to be.

stories.head: The problem with AI doing exactly what you ask
stories.plain: AI agents cause damage not by going rogue but by pursuing a poorly defined objective with high efficiency. The piece sets out a practical governance framework for writing agent objectives that don't produce unintended outcomes — essential reading for anyone deploying automated decisioning in live campaigns.

stories.head: Who owns your AI agents after they launch?
stories.plain: Once an AI agent is live, ownership typically falls in a gap between marketing, IT, and legal. This piece proposes clear accountability structures covering maintenance, oversight, and retirement of agents — directly relevant as more teams deploy agentic tools without formalising who is responsible when things go wrong.

month.skicker: 30-day synthesis · the shape underneath the feed

themes.head: Agentic AI Takes the Wheel — and the Liability
body: Every major platform — HubSpot, Salesforce, Stonly, Vibe, MoEngage — is rebuilding around AI agents that act autonomously, not just assist. HubSpot rebuilt its entire platform on this premise; Salesforce is betting CRM depth gives its agents an edge that pure-AI rivals lack.

But autonomy creates a governance gap nobody has answered cleanly yet. Who owns the agent after it launches? Decisions about approval chains, rollback rights, & accountability structures are now as urgent as the technology itself — and most teams haven't made them.

themes.head: AI Is Becoming the Consumer's Agent, Not Yours
body: AI assistants are now advising shoppers — and sometimes actively recommending against a brand's product. ChatGPT Ads entering the mix signals that the same models giving purchase advice will also carry paid placements, creating an obvious tension between editorial & commercial signals.

This flips the classic funnel: the AI layer sits between brand & buyer, filtering or reframing messages before a human ever sees them. Marketers who optimise only for their own channels are missing the most important new gatekeeper in the purchase journey.

themes.head: Speed Without Process Reform Breaks Everything Faster
body: A sharp cluster of analysis this month converges on a single warning: AI amplifies existing dysfunction. Faster execution of a broken briefing process, a misaligned automation trigger, or an under-contextualised campaign doesn't fix the problem — it scales it.

The implication is that process redesign must precede AI deployment, not follow it. Articles on automation needing more context & AI doing exactly what you ask (to bad effect) both point to the same root cause: organisations measuring AI output against speed rather than business outcomes.

themes.head: Platform Consolidation Wars Reshape the Stack
body: The CDP category is fracturing beyond recognition as CRM, data warehouse, & agent-orchestration layers absorb its functions. Simultaneously, Salesforce & HubSpot are racing to be the single AI-native operating system for go-to-market teams, leaving point solutions fighting for shelf space.

Stensul's move into governed creation on Salesforce Marketing Cloud Next, Causaly's embedding in Microsoft Copilot, & Vibe adding agent access to CTV all follow the same logic: surface your capability inside the platform that controls workflow, or become invisible. Stack decisions made today will be very hard to unwind.
ev: MarTech Series · Stensul on Salesforce MC Next
MarTech Series · Causaly in Microsoft Copilot

themes.head: Measuring AI Against the Wrong Goal Wastes the Investment
body: A recurring signal across editorial & vendor launches alike: companies are benchmarking AI on activity metrics — outputs produced, hours saved, content generated — rather than business outcomes like revenue influence or customer retention. Toggl's Time Intelligence launch makes the point from the opposite direction, turning time-tracking data into real decisions rather than productivity theatre.

Getting measurement right matters because it determines where AI investment flows next. Teams that reframe success criteria around outcomes — not volume — will compound their advantage; those optimising for the wrong signal will scale activity that doesn't move the business.
ev: MarTech · Measuring AI against wrong goal

month.takeaway: The month's news collectively signals that the bottleneck has shifted from AI capability to human judgment — on governance, process design, measurement, & platform allegiance — and the teams that sort those questions first will dictate the next cycle.
